title: Shock: How the Body Copes, and What the PCP Adds
next: Chapter 21, Lesson 2: Controlling bleeding, giving fluids, and the four types of shock

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already stop bleeding, give oxygen, keep patients warm and transport fast. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Understand why shock happens and how the body compensates
  2. Recognize shock before the blood pressure drops
  3. Know what the PCP adds in the BC hypovolemia protocol, and what's new to watch out for

Textbook: Chapter 21, PDF pages 1738–1811
slides.say: Welcome to class. You're all EMRs already, so you know the basics of bleeding control: direct pressure, a tourniquet when you need one, oxygen, keeping the patient warm, and moving fast. Now that you're practising as a PCP, more is expected of you. You need to understand why shock happens, so you can spot it early and explain your decisions. And you have new tools, like IV access, fluids, and a new drug, that come with new responsibilities. Today we'll cover three things: the physiology of shock, how to recognize it before the blood pressure drops, and exactly what the PCP adds in the BC hypovolemia protocol.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎来上课。你们都已经是 EMR，止血的基本功都会：直接压迫、必要时上止血带、给氧、保暖、快速转运。现在以 PCP 身份执业，要求更高：你要理解休克为什么发生，才能更早识别，也能说清自己的决定。你还有了新工具，比如静脉通路、补液和一种新药，也带来新的责任。今天讲三件事：休克的生理机制；怎么在血压掉之前认出休克；BC 低血容量流程里 PCP 具体多做什么。

slides.title: What is shock?
slides.body:
Inadequate tissue perfusion

Cells don't get enough oxygen, and waste isn't carried away.

  • Shock is a state, not a single disease
  • Most common cause in trauma: bleeding
  • Early signs are the body protecting the brain and blood pressure
slides.say: Let's start with the definition. Shock is inadequate tissue perfusion. In plain words, blood is not delivering enough oxygen to the cells, and it's not carrying their waste away. Think of the body as a city, and the blood as delivery trucks. If there aren't enough trucks, or the roads are blocked, the shops start running out of supplies. Shock is a state, not one disease, and in trauma the most common cause is bleeding. Here's the key idea for a PCP: the fast heart rate and cool skin you see early on are not the problem itself. They are the body fighting to protect the brain and the blood pressure.
slides.sayZh: 先说定义：休克是组织灌注不足。白话说，血液没把足够的氧送到细胞，也没把废物运走。把身体想成一座城市，血液是送货卡车；卡车不够或路堵了，商店就断货。休克是一种状态，不是一种病，创伤里最常见的原因是出血。作为 PCP 要抓住一个关键：早期看到的心跳快、皮肤凉，本身不是问题，而是身体在拼命保护大脑和血压。

slides.title: The three parts of circulation
slides.body:
Pumpthe heartfails → cardiogenic
Fluidblood, body fluidtoo little → hypovolemic
Pipesblood vesselstoo wide → distributive

One more: the flow is blocked → obstructive (cardiac tamponade, tension pneumothorax, massive pulmonary embolism)
slides.say: To understand any kind of shock, remember the three parts of circulation: the pump, the fluid, and the pipes. The pump is the heart; if it fails, for example after a big heart attack, that's cardiogenic shock. The fluid is the blood and body fluid; if the patient loses blood or water, that's hypovolemic shock, and bleeding belongs here. The pipes are the blood vessels; if they suddenly open too wide, there isn't enough blood to fill them. That's distributive shock, like anaphylaxis, sepsis, or a spinal cord injury. And if the flow is blocked, as in cardiac tamponade or a tension pneumothorax, it's obstructive shock. This matters more for you now, because as a PCP your treatment, especially fluids, depends on which part is failing.
slides.sayZh: 理解任何休克，记住循环三要素：泵、容量、管道。泵是心脏，泵坏了（比如大面积心梗）叫心源性休克。容量是血液和体液，丢血丢水叫低血容量性休克，出血属于这一类。管道是血管，突然大面积扩张、血装不满，叫分布性休克，比如过敏、脓毒症、脊髓损伤。血流被堵住，比如心包填塞、张力性气胸，叫梗阻性休克。现在这点对你更重要，因为作为 PCP，你的处置，尤其是补液，取决于是哪个零件出了问题。

slides.title: How the body copes: compensation
slides.body:
BP starts to fall→baroreceptors notice→sympathetic system fires
  • Heart beats faster and harder
  • Peripheral vessels constrict (skin turns pale and cool first)
  • Hormones (renin–angiotensin, ADH) hold on to salt and water
  • Blood is redirected to the heart, brain, and lungs

Brain and spinal cord tolerate only 4–6 minutes without blood; kidneys about 45 minutes; muscle about 2 hours.
slides.say: When blood volume starts to drop, pressure sensors called baroreceptors, in the aortic arch and the carotid sinus, notice first. They signal the brain, and the sympathetic nervous system kicks in. The heart beats faster and harder. The vessels in the skin and muscles tighten, which is why the skin turns pale and cool first. Hormones make the kidneys hold on to salt and water. And blood is redirected toward the heart, brain, and lungs. Why that order? Because the brain only tolerates four to six minutes without blood, while muscle can last about two hours. This whole response is called compensation, and when it works, the blood pressure stays normal. That's exactly why shock is so easy to miss.
slides.sayZh: 血容量开始下降时，主动脉弓和颈动脉窦的压力感受器最先察觉，通知大脑，交感神经启动。心跳更快更有力；皮肤和肌肉的血管收紧，所以皮肤最先变白变凉；激素让肾脏保水保钠；血流被引向心、脑、肺。为什么这样排序？因为大脑只能撑四到六分钟没血，肌肉能撑大约两小时。这一整套反应叫代偿，代偿有效时血压保持正常，这正是休克难认的原因。

slides.title: What compensated shock looks like
slides.body:
• Restless, anxious, "something is wrong" ← earliest
  • Fast, weak pulse
  • Skin pale, cool, and clammy; thirst, nausea
  • Fast breathing
  • Narrowing pulse pressure
  • Blood pressure: normal!
slides.say: So what does compensated shock look like in front of you? The earliest sign is often a subtle change in mental status: the patient is restless or anxious, and some say they feel that something bad is about to happen. Then you'll see a fast, weak pulse, skin that is pale, cool, and clammy, thirst, nausea, and faster breathing. As a PCP, also look at the pulse pressure, the gap between the systolic and diastolic numbers. When that gap narrows, the body is squeezing its vessels to hold the pressure up. And here is the dangerous part: the blood pressure may be completely normal. Never feel reassured just because the blood pressure looks fine.
slides.sayZh: 代偿期病人在你面前是什么样？最早常是神志的细微变化：烦躁、焦虑，有人说觉得要出事了。然后是脉搏快而弱，皮肤苍白湿冷，口渴、恶心、呼吸快。作为 PCP，还要看脉压，也就是收缩压和舒张压之间的差距；差距变窄，说明身体在收紧血管撑住血压。危险在于：这时血压可能完全正常，千万别因为血压正常就放心。

slides.q: Which sign usually appears FIRST in hypovolemic shock?
slides.say: Let's pause for a question. Which sign usually appears first in hypovolemic shock? A, falling blood pressure. B, restlessness and anxiety. C, dilated pupils. D, decreased urine output. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 停一下考考你：低血容量性休克最早出现的征象通常是哪个？A 血压下降；B 烦躁焦虑；C 瞳孔散大；D 尿量减少。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B, restlessness and anxiety. Subtle changes in mental status often come first, because the brain is very sensitive to a drop in perfusion. Falling blood pressure is a late sign; it means compensation is failing. Dilated pupils belong to decompensated shock, and decreased urine output takes time to observe, so it's rarely your first clue on scene.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B，烦躁焦虑。神志的细微变化常最先出现，因为大脑对灌注下降最敏感。血压下降是晚期征象，说明代偿撑不住了；瞳孔散大属于失代偿期；尿量减少要观察一段时间，现场很少是第一条线索。

slides.title: Three phases: the tennis score
slides.body:
Compensatedblood loss about 15–30%BP normal
Decompensatedblood loss > 30%BP starts to fall
Irreversiblethe memory aid says > 40%only known in hindsight

Memory aid: 15, 30, 40, like a tennis score.
slides.say: Shock has three phases, and the textbook gives a nice memory aid: the tennis score, fifteen, thirty, forty. With about fifteen to thirty percent blood loss, the patient is in compensated shock, and the blood pressure holds. Above thirty percent, they move into decompensated shock, and the blood pressure starts to fall. The memory aid links more than forty percent with irreversible shock. But the book also admits that irreversible shock can only be judged afterwards, when the patient doesn't respond to treatment. So on scene, as long as the patient has vital signs, treat them as someone you can save.
slides.sayZh: 休克分三期，口诀是网球比分：十五、三十、四十。失血约百分之十五到三十是代偿期，血压撑得住；超过三十进入失代偿期，血压开始掉；口诀把超过四十对应不可逆期。但书里也承认，不可逆只能事后判断，就是病人对治疗没反应。所以现场只要有生命体征，就当作能救回来的病人处理。

slides.title: Blood pressure falls last
slides.body:
Don't wait for low BP to think of shock

  • Low BP means compensation has already failed
  • Infants and young children can lose almost half their blood before BP drops
  • Radial pulse barely palpable → systolic BP is falling fast
  • Mental status = best sign of brain perfusion
slides.say: This is the most important sentence of the lesson: don't wait for a low blood pressure before you think of shock. By the time you measure hypotension, compensation has already failed. Children are even more extreme; infants can compensate until they've lost almost half of their blood, and then they crash suddenly. On scene, your hands and eyes work faster than the cuff. If the radial pulse is barely palpable, even in a patient who is still talking, the systolic pressure is falling fast. Treat it as decompensated shock. And mental status is your best sign of how well the brain is perfused.
slides.sayZh: 这是整节课最重要的一句：别等血压掉了才想到休克。测到低血压时，代偿已经失败。小孩更极端，婴幼儿可以撑到失血接近一半，然后突然垮掉。现场你的手和眼比血压计快：桡动脉几乎摸不到，哪怕病人还在说话，也说明收缩压正快速下降，要按失代偿处理。神志是脑灌注最好的指标。

slides.title: How much blood does a person have?
slides.body:
Blood volume ≈ 6–8% of body weight

  • 80 kg adult ≈ 4.8–6.4 L
  • Adult loses > 1 L: heart rate and breathing ↑, BP ↓
  • One femur fracture can bleed ≥ 1 L; a pelvic fracture > 2 L
  • A 1-year-old has only about 800 mL in total
slides.say: Here are a few numbers to help you estimate blood loss. Blood makes up about six to eight percent of body weight, so an eighty-kilogram adult has roughly four point eight to six point four liters. When an adult loses more than one liter, you'll see a faster heart rate, faster breathing, and a falling blood pressure. A single femur fracture can bleed a liter or more, and a pelvic fracture can bleed more than two liters, all hidden inside. Be extra careful with children: a one-year-old has only about eight hundred milliliters of blood in total. As a PCP you'll use numbers like these to judge how much fluid a patient may need.
slides.sayZh: 几个估算失血的数字：血约占体重的百分之六到八，八十公斤成人大约四点八到六点四升。成人失血超过一升，会出现心率快、呼吸快、血压下降。一处股骨骨折可失血一升以上，骨盆骨折可超过两升，而且都藏在里面。小孩要格外小心，一岁小孩全身只有约八百毫升血。作为 PCP，你会用这些数字判断病人可能需要多少液体。

slides.title: EMR vs PCP: the BC hypovolemia protocol
slides.body:
Use it for hypovolemia + systolic < 90 + other signs of shock (or burns > 20% BSA); may start earlier if shock is expected from the mechanism.

All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • Control external bleeding
  • Splint the pelvis / fractures if indicated
  • Lay the patient supine
  • Keep warm, prevent heat loss
  • Oxygen to SpO₂ ≥ 94%

PCP adds (en route or if delayed)

  • Vascular access (IV)
  • Fluid bolus 20 mL/kg, max 2 L
  • Reassess every 500 mL
  • Consider TXA for shock from blood loss or hidden bleeding
slides.say: Here is the BC hypovolemia protocol, and it shows exactly how your job changes. You use it for a patient with low blood volume, a systolic pressure under ninety, and other signs of shock, or burns over twenty percent of the body. You may start it earlier if the mechanism tells you shock is coming. The left column is everything you already do as an EMR: control the bleeding, splint the pelvis or fractures, lay the patient flat, keep them warm, and give oxygen to keep the saturation at ninety-four percent or higher. The right column is new for you. On the way to hospital, or if there's a delay, the PCP starts an IV, gives a fluid bolus of twenty millilitres per kilogram up to two litres, reassessing every five hundred millilitres, and considers TXA.
slides.sayZh: 这是 BC 的低血容量流程，正好说明你的工作怎么变了。适用于血容量低、收缩压低于九十、并有其他休克征象的病人，或烧伤面积超过百分之二十；如果受伤机制提示休克即将发生，可以更早启动。左栏是你作为 EMR 本来就做的：控制出血、固定骨盆或骨折、平卧、保暖、给氧使血氧维持在九十四以上。右栏是新的：在去医院的路上或现场有延误时，PCP 开静脉通路，按每公斤二十毫升补液、最多两升、每五百毫升复评一次，并考虑使用 TXA。

slides.q: You're a PCP with a hypotensive trauma patient. Bleeding is controlled. Transport time is 25 minutes. What is the best plan?
options: Start the IV on scene before you move the patient
Splint, keep warm, give oxygen, start transport, then start the IV en route
Give 2 L of fluid quickly, then reassess
Wait on scene for an ALS unit to start the IV
slides.say: Let's try a PCP decision. You're a PCP with a hypotensive trauma patient. The bleeding is controlled, and your transport time is twenty-five minutes. What's the best plan? A, start the IV on scene before you move the patient. B, splint, keep the patient warm, give oxygen, start transport, then start the IV en route. C, give two litres of fluid quickly, then reassess. D, wait on scene for an ALS unit to start the IV. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来一道 PCP 决策题。你是 PCP，面前是一位低血压的创伤病人，出血已控制，转运时间二十五分钟。最好的方案是什么？A 先在现场开好静脉再搬病人；B 固定、保暖、给氧、出发，路上再开静脉；C 先快速输两升液体再复评；D 在现场等 ALS 来开静脉。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. The BC protocol puts the IV en route, or on scene only if there's a delay, so you never hold a bleeding patient on scene just to start a line. A wastes time the patient doesn't have. C is wrong because the bolus is twenty millilitres per kilogram up to two litres, and you reassess after every five hundred millilitres, not after two litres. D delays definitive care for something you can do yourself.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。BC 流程把开静脉放在转运途中，只有在有延误时才在现场开，所以绝不能为了开静脉把出血病人留在现场。A 浪费病人没有的时间；C 错在补液是每公斤二十毫升、最多两升，而且每五百毫升就要复评，不是输完两升再看；D 为了一件你自己能做的事拖延了确定性治疗。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• Never delay transport to start an IV
  • More fluid isn't always better: saline doesn't carry oxygen and dilutes clotting factors — reassess every 500 mL
  • Head injury is different: BC wants systolic > 120, glucose 4.0–8.0 mmol/L
  • TXA: not if > 3 hours since injury, age < 12, or isolated head injury
  • TXA dose: 2 g IV push over 1 minute — faster can drop the BP
slides.say: Now the things you never had to worry about as an EMR. First, an IV is never a reason to stay on scene. Second, more fluid is not always better. The book reminds us that saline doesn't carry oxygen and it dilutes clotting factors, so give it in steps and reassess every five hundred millilitres. Third, head injury is the exception. For a traumatic brain injury, BC wants a systolic pressure above one hundred twenty and a blood sugar between four and eight. Fourth, TXA has hard stops: don't give it more than three hours after the injury, under age twelve, or for an isolated head injury. The BC dose is two grams by IV push over one minute; pushing it faster can drop the blood pressure.
slides.sayZh: 现在讲你当 EMR 时不用操心、现在要注意的事。第一，开静脉永远不是留在现场的理由。第二，补液不是越多越好：书里提醒生理盐水不带氧，还会稀释凝血因子，所以要分步给、每五百毫升复评。第三，颅脑外伤是例外：BC 要求收缩压高于一百二十、血糖在四到八之间。第四，TXA 有硬禁忌：受伤超过三小时、未满十二岁、单纯颅脑外伤都不能给。BC 剂量是两克静脉推注、一分钟推完，推太快会让血压下降。

slides.title: The lethal triad of trauma
slides.body:
Coldhypothermia
Clottingcoagulopathy
Acidacidosis

Each one makes the others worse. Response: stop the bleeding, keep the patient warm, don't overdo the saline.
slides.say: One idea ties all of this together: the lethal triad of trauma. Hypothermia, coagulopathy, and acidosis; in simple words, cold, poor clotting, and acid. They make each other worse. A cold patient clots poorly, more bleeding means more acid, and acid makes clotting worse again. As an EMR you already fight the cold with blankets. As a PCP you now also control what goes into the vein, and that's where this matters most: large amounts of cold, slightly acidic saline can feed all three parts of the triad. Warm the patient, warm your fluids if you can, and give only what the protocol and your reassessment call for.
slides.sayZh: 有一个概念把这些串起来：创伤致死三联征——低体温、凝血障碍、酸中毒，简单说就是冷、凝、酸，三者互相加重：一冷凝血就差，出血更多酸就更重，酸又让凝血更差。作为 EMR，你已经会用毯子保暖。作为 PCP，你现在还掌控着输进静脉的东西，这正是关键：大量冰冷、偏酸的生理盐水会同时加重三联征的三个部分。给病人保暖，能加温就给液体加温，只给流程和复评需要的量。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Compensated shock has a normal BP: watch mental status, pulse, skin, pulse pressure
  2. The PCP adds IV, fluids, and TXA — en route, 20 mL/kg up to 2 L, reassess every 500 mL
  3. New watch-outs: never delay transport; TBI wants systolic > 120; know TXA's hard stops

Next: controlling bleeding, giving fluids, and the four types of shock
slides.say: Let's wrap up with three things to remember. One: in compensated shock the blood pressure can be completely normal, so watch mental status, the pulse, the skin, and the pulse pressure. Two: as a PCP, you add vascular access, fluids, and TXA. Do it en route, give twenty millilitres per kilogram up to two litres, and reassess every five hundred. Three: the new watch-outs. Never delay transport for an IV, aim for a systolic above one hundred twenty in a head injury, and know TXA's hard stops. Next lesson, we'll look at bleeding control in more detail and at how each of the four types of shock is managed. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 收尾三句话。一，代偿期休克血压可以完全正常，要看神志、脉搏、皮肤和脉压。二，作为 PCP 你多了静脉通路、补液和 TXA：路上做，每公斤二十毫升、最多两升，每五百毫升复评。三，新的注意事项：别为开静脉耽误转运；颅脑外伤目标收缩压一百二十以上；记住 TXA 的硬禁忌。下节课详细讲止血，以及四种休克各怎么处理。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
